record.paper_title: Theoretical descriptions of compound-nuclear reactions: open problems & challenges
record.original_question: What practical approximation methods can reproduce the weak-absorption compound-nucleus cross sections and width-fluctuation effects that are treated by the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble reference approach, while avoiding the computational cost of the full closed-form calculation and improving approximate expressions for the width-fluctuation correction factor Wcc′?

evidence.quote: However, it requires a computationally expensive calculation of a triple integral that enters the closed-form expression for the average cross section [76].
While the GOE approach is often considered a reference to which other theories should be compared, approximate methods are needed for practical applications.
In recent years, there has been renewed focus on testing various approximate expressions for Wcc′ against the GOE approach [51] and to develop improvements [56].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider statistical compound-nucleus reactions in the regime of weak absorption (small transmission coefficients, many open channels of comparable strength). Within the random-matrix framework, the average reaction cross section between an entrance channel c and an exit channel c' is given exactly by the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (GOE) result of Verbaarschot–Weidenmüller–Zirnbauer:

  ⟨σ_{cc'}⟩ ∝ T_c T_{c'} W_{cc'} + (direct/elastic enhancement terms),

where T_a = 1 − |⟨S_{aa}⟩|² are channel transmission coefficients (S the scattering matrix), and W_{cc'} is the width-fluctuation correction factor. In the GOE approach W_{cc'} is expressed as a triple integral whose numerical evaluation is computationally expensive, especially when many channels (elastic, inelastic, capture, fission, etc.) are open.

Two widely used approximate closed-form expressions for W_{cc'} exist:
 (i) the Moldauer formula, which writes 1 + 2δ_{cc'}/ν_c times an integral over a product (1 + 2T_a τ / ν_a)^{−1/2} with channel-degree-of-freedom parameters ν_a fitted to the GOE;
 (ii) the HRTW (Hofmann–Richert–Tepel–Weidenmüller) prescription based on elastic enhancement factors.

Problem. Construct a practical approximation scheme for the average compound-nucleus cross sections and the width-fluctuation correction factor W_{cc'} in the weak-absorption regime that:

 (a) reproduces the GOE benchmark values of W_{cc'} (and hence ⟨σ_{cc'}⟩) to controlled accuracy uniformly over the physically relevant range of transmission coefficients {T_a} and number of open channels;
 (b) avoids evaluation of the triple integral in the closed-form GOE expression, in particular by replacing it with closed-form, low-dimensional, or otherwise inexpensive expressions;
 (c) improves quantitatively on the existing Moldauer and HRTW approximations for W_{cc'}, including in regimes (e.g., presence of strongly absorbing or direct-reaction channels, near-threshold channels, or channels with strongly disparate T_a) where these approximations are known to deviate from the GOE result.

Formalize the construction by specifying the functional form of the proposed W_{cc'}, prescribing how its parameters are determined from {T_a}, and proving (or numerically demonstrating) error bounds against the exact GOE triple-integral expression.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has provided substantial improvements but no definitive closed-form replacement. Kawano, Talou, and Weidenmüller (Phys. Rev. C 92, 044617 (2015); Phys. Rev. C 94, 014612 (2016)) and Hilaire–Lagrange–Koning (Ann. Phys. 306, 209 (2003)) systematically compared Moldauer and HRTW against the GOE triple integral and found Moldauer with reparametrized channel degrees-of-freedom ν_a to be the closest to GOE. Kawano (Phys. Rev. C 99, 024621 (2019)) further refined Moldauer's parametrization using GOE references. Recent work (e.g., arXiv:2410.01074, 2024) continues to refine these approximations for specific applications such as gamma branching ratios. The problem is therefore partially solved: improved Moldauer-type approximations exist and are widely used, but the question of an optimal, provably accurate, GOE-equivalent approximation across all regimes remains an active area of research.

status_evidence.title: Random-matrix approach to the statistical compound nuclear reaction
status_evidence.snippet: Implements exact GOE expression and compares to Moldauer/HRTW approximations.
status_evidence.claim: Exact GOE-based W_{cc'} computations are now available for benchmarking approximations.

status_evidence.title: Comparisons between various width fluctuation correction factors
status_evidence.snippet: Moldauer's approximation is closest to the GOE value; recommended for practical applications.
status_evidence.claim: Moldauer's approximation has been identified as best among the standard practical approximations to W_{cc'}.

status_evidence.title: Transmission coefficients in compound-nucleus reaction calculations
status_evidence.snippet: Reparametrizes the channel degree-of-freedom ν_a in Moldauer's model to better reproduce GOE.
status_evidence.claim: Improved Moldauer-type approximations have been developed against GOE references.

status_evidence.title: Correcting for neutron width fluctuations in Hauser-Feshbach gamma branching ratios
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) refinements of width fluctuation treatments for specific reaction observables.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues to improve approximations to W_{cc'} for practical use.
